ledger: ARW House baby sunscreen claim ledger
rule: Only claims with status=verified may be published. Every number must be reproducible by the script named in `method`. Wording in `publishable_sentence` is the maximum strength allowed.

claims.claim: Among unique mineral-active baby sunscreen formulations on DailyMed, 49 of 148 (33.1%) contain at least one UV-absorbing excipient not listed as an active ingredient.
claims.publishable_sentence: About 1 in 3 baby sunscreens sold as mineral-only in the US also contain an ingredient that absorbs UV light but is not listed as an active ingredient.
claims.population: category=sunscreen AND baby_labeled=true; deduplicated by formulation_hash (391 registrations -> 332 unique formulations); actives contain ZnO and/or TiO2 and no FDA chemical filter
claims.source: arwfamily/tinysafe-dailymed-scraper-v2 data/canonical/us_sunscreens.jsonl, snapshot last_seen 2026-10-05 (13,326 rows, of which 6,537 category=sunscreen)
claims.method: scripts/verify_ledger.py US-HID-001 (independent regex on inactive ingredient names; does NOT use the pipeline flag has_hidden_chemical_filter)
claims.supersedes: 45 of 144 (IG series, Aug 2026) — pipeline flag missed ethylhexyl methoxycrylene in 4 ZnO+TiO2 products (Johnson's Baby Mineral SPF30, Aveeno Baby/Kids Daily Moisture Face, one other)
claims.legal_framing: Not a violation: these excipients are not FDA-recognised sunscreen actives, so listing them as actives would itself be non-compliant. The finding is about the labeling system, not about any brand.
known_limits: baby_labeled classifier also matches company names (e.g. BABYFACE LLC, Baby Bubba soap); excluding the doubtful cases moves the ratio to ~33-34%, sentence unchanged
Whether each excipient materially contributes to SPF is product-specific and not measured here; the sentence says 'absorbs UV light', not 'boosts SPF'
claims.blocker: Repo audit 2026-10-08: (1) category classifier is title-substring based — baby sunscreens labeled TINTED/other are excluded from category=sunscreen; (2) baby_labeled matches labeler names and misses Mustela/Pipette/Babo/Attitude Little Ones; (3) hidden-absorber list here omits diethylhexyl syringylidenemalonate, polysilicone-15, benzylidene dimethoxydimethylindanone. Numerator and denominator will both move. Do NOT publish until recomputed on a hand-reviewed baby list.

claims.population: same as US-HID-001

claims.claim: 144 of 501 ARTG-listed sunscreens in the dataset list bemotrizinol as an active; 11 of them are baby/kids-named (Banana Boat Baby/Kids, Cancer Council Kids).
claims.publishable_sentence: In Australia, bemotrizinol is already an active ingredient in at least 144 listed sunscreens, including at least 11 sold for babies and kids.
claims.supersedes: '145' used in chat on 2026-10-08 (145 is the zinc oxide count)
claims.SCOPE_WARNING: The 501 products come from an ARTG export of a keyword search for 'sunscreen' (export footer: SearchValues contains 'sunscreen', 2026-08-21) — not a census. Use 'at least N'; no market percentages.
claims.note_bemt_name: TGA's own approved name is BEMOTRIZINOL; no name-mapping issue.

claims.claim: FDA Final Administrative Order OTC000039 (issued 2026-06-10, corrected 2026-08-10, effective 2026-08-09) added bemotrizinol to OTC Monograph M020: up to 6%, GRASE for adults and children 6 months and older; DSM receives 18 months of marketing exclusivity from the effective date; may not be combined with aminobenzoic acid or trolamine salicylate. Permitted dosage forms: oil, lotion, cream, gel, butter, paste, ointment, stick, and spray only as pump or bag-on-valve; NOT permitted: propellant aerosol sprays and powders.
claims.todo: Order PDF read 2026-10-08 (dosage forms, combinations, exclusivity confirmed). Done.
claims.credit: Dosage-form restriction first flagged by Muse package (2026-10-08); verified against Venable analysis. Confirm in order PDF text.

claims.claim: FDA Final Administrative Order OTC000008-1 (signed 2026-09-08, issued 2026-09-11) amends M020 to remove aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and trolamine salicylate as sunscreen active ingredients, effective 2027-09-11 (or later if disputed).
claims.publishable_sentence: In September 2026 the FDA finalized the removal of PABA and trolamine salicylate from the list of permitted US sunscreen ingredients.
claims.precision_rule: Until 2027-09-11 both remain listed M020 actives. Say 'removal finalized, effective 2027-09-11', never 'banned' or 'no longer permitted'. The FDA Q&A page lists 2026-09-10; the order PDF says issued 2026-09-11 — the order PDF governs.
claims.credit: First flagged by Muse package (2026-10-08); verified on FDA Q&A page.

claims.claim: Jurisdiction matrix for the 20 v1 filters: every cell carries its source document URL; AU caps parsed only from sentences about the ingredient's own concentration.
